newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 ends with modest losses.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 ends with modest losses.

text.p: UK's FTSE 100 ended with modest losses on Thursday, as concerns about the fate of EMU in the wake of the Bundesbank row with Bonn and worries about the outcome of the French elections were softened by a late advance in the U.S. bond market, dealers and analysts said.

"The problems in Germany and concerns about the French election are all reasons for the market to go lower," said one senior dealer. "But we've seen some selective buying, albeit on tiny volume. The market's performance has been quite encouraging."
The blue chip share index ended 5.2 points lower at 4,672.3, though advancers led decliners 56 to 42.

Yet volume remained light, with only 641.1 million shares registered by 1535 GMT, boosted by a share buyback by Royal & Sun Alliance Group Plc and a five million share placing of Alliance & Leicester Plc stock.
A directionless start of Wall Street provided little impetus for UK shares. The Dow opened steady and was down about 25 points when London markets closed.
Dealers and analysts attributed the lack of trading not just to many fund managers taking extended holiday this week, but also to the political uncertainty in Europe.

"People are just standing back, waiting and watching what happens with the French elections and how this spat with the Bundesbank works out," said stock strategist David Aserkoff of Credit Suisse First Boston.

Initial weakness in the market reflected nervousness over European unrest. News the Bundesbank rejected the German government's decision to revalue gold assets and worries over the second round of voting in France took a toll on sentiment.
The Bundesbank on Thursday said its rejection of Bonn's intentions to revalue its reserves may be enough to block a required law change in parliament.

Elsewhere, the French stock market slipped back after an early attempt to rebound from Wednesday's steep losses sustained amid rumours that private polls showed the Socialists well-placed for victory in Sunday's election.
UK equities could be beneficiaries of European instability as investors flock to UK assets as a safehaven, Askerkoff said.

UK stocks shrugged off data released earlier showing the UK's global trade deficit was 671 million stg against expectations of 900 million, and the April non-EU trade deficit of 335 million against forecasts of 600 million.
Among individual stocks, shares Smiths Industries Plc shares added 12p to 780-1/2p after analysts took a positive view following an upbeat company visit on Wednesday.
"Basically the inference was that the aerospace business will surprise on the upside in the next two years. The industry in general is going ballistic," said one analyst.
Shares in Burmah Castrol Plc rose 29p to 1065 in a generally weaker oil sector after broker SocGen repeated its "buy" recommendation for the oil company.
Shares in Siebe Plc advanced 13-1/2p to 962 after the UK engineering group posted a larger-than-expected increase in its full year profits.
Bank shares, runaway outperformers in recent months, fell back as investors took profits, dealer said.
The June 2 listing of the Halifax Building Society has boosted the financial sector as institutional investors are expected to build stakes in the Halifax, dealer said.
Abbey National shares fell 25p to 902, while shares in Barclays Plc tumbled 30-1/2p to 1218. Shares in the Royal Bank of Scotland shed 19p to 615-1/2.
Among second-liners, shares in London International Group Plc added 12-1/2p to 169p, after the condom to rubber glove maker promised "double-digit earnings growth" in the next few years.
LIG reported a 12.6 percent rise in pre-tax profit to 29.5 million stg in the year ending on March 31, 1997.
The company added that LIG's three-year restructuring was now over and the company was poised to enter a new stage of growth.
--Debra Sherman, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
